issues.description: The solution defines a subroutine named 'write_pixel' that computes and writes the pixel, but the program's call site (and the template's expected subroutine) uses the name 'set_pixel'. The problem statement also specifies implementing 'set_pixel' with a given calling convention. This name/signature mismatch will cause an unresolved symbol / link error and prevents the student from following the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's subroutine match the expected name and calling convention. Either rename 'write_pixel' to 'set_pixel' and ensure it preserves registers per the problem statement, or change the call site to 'call write_pixel' and update the problem/template consistently. Ensure the final implementation matches the specification in problem_statement.md (set_pixel: x in EAX, y in EBX, color in ECX, only EAX may be modified).

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the subroutine name set_pixel, but the reference solution implements the functionality under the name write_pixel. This mismatch (set_pixel vs write_pixel) makes it unclear which symbol students should implement or modify and breaks the direct mapping from the task description to the example implementation. Inside the solution file the implemented routine is write_pixel while main still calls set_pixel, amplifying the confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the pixel-setting routine across all artifacts. Rename the solution's write_pixel label to set_pixel (or update the template/problem to use write_pixel) so the subroutine implementation name matches the name used in the task description and the calls in main.
